 Declassification of pardon records not unusual, says PM
 Friday, 20 Nov 2026
 share 
 bookmark 
 SHENZHEN: It is not unusual for confidential Pardons Board documents to be declassified if they have been challenged through court proceedings, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
 He said applications or challenges through the courts invol­ving such documents could normally lead to their declassification, while the date of implementation would be determined later.
 “The original documents are indeed confidential, but usually, if they are brought to court, they are declassified. That was also the case in my previous case.
 “They were initially classified, but once there was a court challenge. In my case, I did not challenge the Board’s decision; I challenged the process,” he told a press conference after attending the 2026 Apec Economic Leaders’ Meeting here yesterday.
 Anwar said further queries or concerns on the matter could be raised with the Cabinet, Bernama reported.
 He was responding to reports that the minutes of a Federal Territories Pardons Board meeting, which discussed granting house arrest to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak, had been declassified.
